summary: GridCraft is a spreadsheet app, like Microsoft Excel. It opens and saves .xlsx files. It can also work from typed commands.
use_cases: Make a formatted report with charts from a monthly CSV export.
Calculate shares and changes with COUNTIFS formulas. The results update when the data changes.
Print a summary sheet to PDF automatically every night.
Check 1 number fast. Get 1 answer from a saved workbook with 1 typed formula.
story: GridCraft calculated the numbers for Signal & Noise 2026. It imported 387 posts from a CSV file. Each post has 1 theme and 1 tone label: positive, neutral or negative. COUNTIFS formulas counted the posts for each month and theme. Other formulas calculated the share of the conversation and the % negative from these counts. GridCraft then drew 3 charts and printed the Summary sheet to PDF. WordCraft and PdfCraft used 2 of these charts.
recipe_note: Build the workbook from a list of steps. Print the Summary sheet to PDF. Check 1 number.

assets.caption: The Summary sheet shows the share of the conversation per month, the tone per theme and 3 charts.
assets.description: GridCraft printed the finished Summary sheet to PDF. PdfCraft then made this image from the PDF page.
assets.how: gridcraft-cli run --in signal-noise-2026.xlsx --cmd 'file.exportPdf={"path":"summary.pdf","sheets":"active"}'; pdfcraft-cli render summary.pdf --page 1 --dpi 150 --out summary.png (margins trimmed with PIL)

assets.caption: GridCraft drew these 2 charts. They show the share of the conversation for 4 themes and the share of negative posts.
assets.description: GridCraft drew these charts from the formulas in the workbook. PdfCraft made an image of the PDF page. A short Python script cropped the 2 charts from it.
assets.how: GridCraft file.exportPdf, then pdfcraft-cli render summary.pdf --page 1 --dpi 300; charts cropped and stacked with PIL

assets.caption: The animation shows the workbook in 6 stages: import, count, share, tone, format and charts.
assets.description: GridCraft ran the build to the end of each stage and printed the result to PDF. PdfCraft made an image of each PDF. A short Python script joined the images into a GIF and added captions.
assets.how: For each step N: gridcraft-cli run --script stage_v2_N.jsonl --cmd 'file.exportPdf={...}', then pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 110; frames captioned and joined into a GIF with PIL

assets.caption: The workbook has 3 sheets: Summary with percentages, Counts with COUNTIFS totals, and Posts with the data.
assets.description: GridCraft read the raw CSV file and ran a list of 535 steps. GridCraft wrote every formula, coloured the cells and drew 3 charts.

assets.caption: This 1-page PDF of the Summary sheet is ready to print.
assets.description: GridCraft printed the Summary sheet to an A4 landscape PDF. It added the footer and fitted the sheet to 1 page.

assets.caption: GridCraft answered 4 quick formula checks, for example: 53% of Prices & tokens posts are negative.
assets.description: Each answer comes from 1 typed formula. GridCraft calculated each answer from the saved workbook.

assets.caption: The Posts sheet shows the 387 posts that GridCraft imported from the CSV file as a table.
assets.description: GridCraft imported the CSV file as a formatted table with a frozen header row. GridCraft printed the sheet to PDF. PdfCraft made this image from the PDF.
assets.how: gridcraft-cli run --script stage_v2_1_import.jsonl + file.exportPdf (print area A1:K34); pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 110 (trimmed with PIL)

assets.caption: The Counts sheet shows the COUNTIFS totals behind the percentages.
assets.description: GridCraft counted the posts for each month and theme with COUNTIFS formulas. The Summary sheet calculates its percentages from these counts.
assets.how: gridcraft-cli run --in signal-noise-2026.xlsx --cmd 'sheet.activate={"sheet":"Counts"}' --cmd 'file.exportPdf={...}'; pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 130 (trimmed with PIL)

assets.caption: This web page shows the cells of the Summary sheet, without the charts.
assets.description: GridCraft saved the Summary sheet as an HTML table. The web page keeps the colours but not the charts.

assets.caption: This list holds the 535 steps that GridCraft did to build the workbook.
assets.description: A small Python program wrote this list of steps. GridCraft read the list and did each step in order.
assets.how: Written by a Python helper (make_script_v2.py); run by gridcraft-cli run --script

headless_notes: All work ran through gridcraft-cli with no window: run, convert, eval, info and cat. GridCraft has no command that saves a sheet as an image. GridCraft printed each sheet to PDF, and pdfcraft-cli render made the PNG. range.fill reads formulas relative to cell A1, so each formula went in cell by cell. Charts need a single block of cells, so 2 small chart-data blocks feed the line and bar charts. In footers, write '&&' for 1 ampersand. The HTML export has no charts.
